passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: If you have a concern about harassment, discrimination, retaliation, safety or any other breach of this handbook, you can raise it in whichever way you are most comfortable with. You can talk to your manager. You can contact the HR Service Desk at hr@ridgeline.example or through HR Portal > Ask HR. For sensitive matters, contact HR Confidential at hr-confidential@ridgeline.example, which only a small HR team can read. You can also call the ethics line on +1 555 0100, available 24/7, with an anonymous option. You never have to raise a concern with the person it is about. When you raise a concern, say what happened, when and where, who was involved and whether anyone else saw it. You don't need proof, and you don't need to be certain that a rule was broken; it is enough that you have a genuine concern. If you prefer, HR can open an HR ticket for you in the HR Confidential queue, with only a minimal summary recorded, and contact you to discuss the details privately.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: Concerns are handled confidentially. Information is shared only with the people who need it to look into and resolve the concern, and HR tells you who that is where it can.

args.query: retaliation protection for raising a concern

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: Ridgeline does not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith or takes part in an investigation. Retaliation is itself a breach of this handbook and is dealt with through the HR process. If you think you are being treated badly because you raised a concern, report it through any route in §6.1.

passages.title: Employee Handbook & Code of Conduct
passages.text: Ridgeline prohibits harassment, discrimination and bullying of any kind. Examples of prohibited conduct include unwelcome comments or jokes about a person's accent, ethnicity, religion, gender, age, disability or appearance; repeated belittling in meetings; unwanted physical contact; and offensive messages or images. This applies in the office, on project sites, at client premises, at work events and online. If you experience or witness conduct like this, you can raise it through any route in §6, and you will be protected from retaliation (§6.3). What matters is the effect of the conduct, not the intention behind it. A remark meant as a joke can still be harassment if it is unwelcome and demeaning, and a pattern of small remarks can be as serious as a single incident. Everyone at Ridgeline is expected to treat colleagues, clients and site workers with respect, to speak up when they see behaviour that crosses the line, and to support colleagues who raise a concern. Managers who become aware of possible harassment must make sure HR knows about it, even if the person affected has not made a formal report.
